title: Pizza dough
intro: Four 250 g dough balls for a soft, airy crust, even in a home oven.

steps.t: Dissolve the yeast in the cold water, add two thirds of the flour and stir into a thick batter.
Add the salt, then the rest of the flour and the oil, and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover the bowl and let it rest for 2 hours at room temperature, away from drafts.
steps.label: Rise

steps.t: Divide into 4 balls of about 250 g and shape them by pulling the surface underneath until taut.
Place them well apart in an oiled container, cover and let them rise for 3 hours, until doubled.
steps.label: Dough balls

steps.t: They're ready to stretch. To use later, keep them in the fridge up to 24 hours and take them out 2 hours before.

tips.t: For more flavor and an airier crust, rest the balls in the fridge overnight (12-24 hours).
Swap the 4 g of fresh yeast for 1.5 g of active dry yeast.

title: Fresh egg pasta
intro: One egg per 100 g of flour: the classic sheet, rolled thin and cut by hand.

steps.t: Mound the flour on a board, make a well and crack the eggs into the center.
Beat the eggs with a fork and draw in the flour from the edges, a little at a time.
Knead with the heel of your hand for 10 minutes, until smooth, firm and elastic.
Wrap in plastic wrap and let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Divide into 4 pieces and roll out with a pin or pasta machine to 1 mm: you should see your hand through it.
Let the sheets dry for 10 minutes on a kitchen towel, until no longer sticky.
steps.label: Drying

steps.t: Roll each sheet up loosely and slice with a knife: 7 mm for tagliatelle, 1.5 cm for pappardelle.
Unroll the ribbons right away, dust with semolina and shape into nests. They cook in 2-3 minutes in salted boiling water.

tips.t: For lasagna and ravioli, stop before cutting and use the whole sheets.
Use 2 whole eggs and 3 yolks for a richer, yellower dough, like Piedmont's tajarin.
Dry the nests for 1 hour, then freeze them on a tray: cook them straight from frozen.

title: Pasta frolla (Italian shortcrust)
intro: Crumbly and lemon-scented, for tarts and cookies: enough for a 24 cm pan.

steps.t: Dice the fridge-cold butter and rub it into the flour and salt with your fingertips until sandy.
Add the powdered sugar and grated lemon zest, then the egg and the yolk.
Knead quickly, only until it comes together: overworked dough bakes up hard.
Flatten into a disc, wrap in plastic and chill for at least 1 hour.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Roll it out between two sheets of baking paper to 4 mm: it's ready to line the pan.
If you're not using it right away, keep it well wrapped in the fridge up to 3 days or frozen for 2 months.

tips.t: For a crostata, line the pan, fill with 350 g of jam and bake at 180 °C for 35 minutes.
Very cold butter and cool hands are what keep the pastry short and crumbly.
Swap the lemon for the seeds of half a vanilla bean or a pinch of cinnamon.

title: Pâte brisée (shortcrust)
intro: Cold butter and a light touch: a flaky, neutral crust for quiches and savory pies.

steps.t: Dice the very cold butter and put it in a bowl with the flour and salt.
Rub it in quickly with your fingertips until you have pea-sized crumbs.
Add the ice water a spoonful at a time and press together without kneading: bits of butter should remain.
Flatten into a disc, wrap in plastic and chill for 1 hour.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Roll out on a floured surface to 3 mm and line a 24 cm pan, pricking the base with a fork.

tips.t: To blind-bake, cover with baking paper and dried beans: 15 minutes at 190 °C, then 10 more uncovered.
Replace 50 g of flour with grated parmesan for richer quiches and vegetable pies.

title: Vegetable broth
intro: About 2 liters of clear, gently sweet broth for risotto, soups and slow cooking.

steps.t: Wash the vegetables. Cut the carrots, celery and leek into large chunks and halve the onion, leaving some skin on for color.
Put everything in a large pot with the whole tomato, parsley, peppercorns, bay leaf and cold water.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then turn the heat down to low.

pressure.t: Close the pressure cooker (fill it no more than two thirds) and bring it up to pressure over high heat.

steps.t: Simmer gently, partly covered, for 1 hour without stirring, so it stays clear.
steps.label: Broth

pressure.t: Once it hisses, lower the heat and cook for 20 minutes, then let the pressure drop naturally.

steps.t: Turn off the heat, add salt and let it rest for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Strain through a fine sieve without pressing the vegetables. Keeps 3 days in the fridge, or freeze in portions.

tips.t: Blend the cooked vegetables with a little olive oil into a soup to serve with croutons.
A parmesan rind simmered in the pot adds depth, though the broth is no longer vegan.
Stud the onion with a clove for a warmer aroma in winter.

title: Chicken stock
intro: About 2 liters of golden, deep-flavored stock for tortellini, soups or risotto.

steps.t: Rinse the chicken and put it in a tall pot with the cold water.
Bring slowly to a boil and skim off the gray foam with a slotted spoon for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Skimming

steps.t: Add the carrot, the onion with its skin, the celery, parsley and peppercorns, and turn the heat to low.
Simmer partly covered for 2 hours 30 minutes: it should barely tremble, never boil hard, so it stays clear.
steps.label: Stock

pressure.t: Close the pressure cooker (no more than two thirds full) and, once it hisses, cook for 45 minutes on low heat.

steps.t: Salt, turn off the heat and strain through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. The meat should fall off the bone.
If you have time, chill it overnight and lift off the solidified fat on top.

tips.t: With tortellini or cappelletti and grated parmesan, it's the Emilian Christmas lunch.
Shred the poached chicken and serve it with salsa verde for a ready-made main.
Freeze it in 250 ml portions: it keeps 3 months, ready for a risotto.

title: Dashi
intro: Japan's essential stock: kombu and bonito flakes, ready in under an hour.

steps.t: Wipe the kombu with a damp cloth but don't wash it: the white powder on the surface is flavor.
Soak it in the cold water in a pot for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Heat over medium-low for about 10 minutes and lift out the kombu as soon as the first small bubbles appear.
steps.label: Kombu

steps.t: Bring to a boil, turn off the heat and add the katsuobushi all at once.
Let it steep for 2 minutes, until the flakes sink.
steps.label: Steep

steps.t: Strain through a sieve lined with paper towel, without squeezing. Use it for miso soup, noodles or eggs.

tips.t: For a vegan dashi, use only kombu and 4 dried shiitake, soaked overnight in the fridge.
Make a second, lighter dashi: simmer the used kombu and flakes in 1 liter of water for 10 minutes.
